1.1: In the land named Uz, there was a man named Job. He was a very godly/righteous man, who greatly respected/revered God and always avoided doing evil things.
1.2: He had seven sons and three daughters.
1.3: He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 1,000 oxen, and 500 female donkeys. He also had many servants. He was the richest man in all the area east [of the Jordan River].
1.4: Each year, Job’s sons made feasts [in their houses] to celebrate their birthdays. Whenever each one made a feast, he would invite [all his brothers and] his three sisters to come and eat together.
1.5: When each celebration ended, Job would summon them. He would get up early in the morning and kill animals and burn them on the altar as sacrifices, one for each of his children. He said to himself, “Perhaps [one of] my sons has sinned and said something evil about God in his heart.”
1.6: One day, the angels came and gathered together in front of Yahweh, and Satan came too.
1.7: Yahweh asked Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan replied, “I have come from the earth, where I been traveling back and forth, seeing what is happening.”
1.8: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you ◄noticed/thought about► my [faithful] servant Job? He is very godly/righteous , he greatly respects/reveres me, and he always avoids doing evil things. There is no one else on the earth like him.”
1.9: Satan replied to Yahweh, “[What you say is true], but Job greatly respects you [only] because of what [you have done for him] .
1.10: You have always protected him and his family and everything that he owns. You have made him very prosperous/rich. He has livestock all over this land.
1.11: But if you take away everything that he has, he will curse you openly. ”
1.12: Yahweh replied to Satan, “◄All right/Okay►, I will permit you to take away everything that he has. But do not harm him.” Then Satan left, [and he prepared to cause many disastrous things to happen to Job].
1.13: One day [after that], Job’s sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the home of their oldest brother.
1.14: While they were doing that, a messenger arrived at Job’s home and said to him, “While your oxen were plowing [the fields] and the donkeys were grazing nearby,
1.15: a group of men from [the] Sheba [area] came and attacked us. They killed all your servants [who were working in the fields] and took away all the oxen and donkeys! I am the only one who escaped to [come and] tell you what happened.”
1.16: While he was still talking to Job, another messenger arrived. He said to Job, “Lightning from the sky struck and killed all the sheep and all the men who were taking care of the sheep! I am the only one who escaped to [come and] tell you [what happened].”
1.17: While he was still talking to Job, another messenger arrived. He said to Job, “Three groups [of robbers/bandits] from Chaldea [land] came and attacked us. They stole all the camels and killed all the men who were taking care of them. I am the only one who escaped to [come and] tell you [what happened].”
1.18: While he was still talking to Job, another messenger arrived and reported this to Job: “Your sons and daughters were feasting in the home of their oldest brother.
1.19: Suddenly a ◄very strong wind/tornado► came from the desert and struck the house. The house collapsed on your sons and daughters and killed them all! I am the only one who escaped to [come and] tell you [what happened].”
1.20: Job stood up, and tore his robe and shaved his head [because he was very sad/grieved]. Then he prostrated himself on the ground [to worship God].
1.21: He said, “When I was born, I had no clothes on. When I die, I will not take any clothes with me. Yahweh gave me [everything that I possessed], and [now] he has taken it all away. But ◄we should/I will► always praise Yahweh [anyway]! ”
1.22: In spite of all these [things that happened to ] Job, [he ] did not sin by saying that what God had done was wrong.

2.1: On another day, the angels came again and gathered together in front of Yahweh, and Satan came too.
2.2: Yahweh asked Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan replied, “I have come from the earth, where I have been traveling back and forth, seeing what is happening.”
2.3: Yahweh asked Satan, “Have you ◄noticed/thought about► my [faithful] servant Job? He is very godly/righteous , he greatly respects/reveres me, and he [always] avoids doing evil things. And he still acts in a very godly/righteous manner, even though you persuaded me to [let you] cause disastrous things to happen to him for no reason.”
2.4: Satan replied to Yahweh, “He praises you only because you bless him . People will give up everything they have to save their own lives.

2.6: Yahweh replied to Satan, “◄All right/Okay►, you may do to him whatever you want to do, but do not cause him to die.”

2.9: His wife said to him, “Are you still trying to ◄be loyal to/faithfully trust in► God? You should curse God, and then you will die.”
2.10: But Job replied, “You talk like people who do not know God talk. ◄Should we accept only the good things that God [does for us]?/We should not accept only the good things that God [does for us].► We should also accept bad things.” So in spite of all these [things that happened to] Job, [he] did not say anything against God.
2.11: Among Job’s friends were Eliphaz from Teman [town], Bildad from Shuah [land] and Zophar from Naamah [land]. When they heard about all the terrible things that had happened to Job, they left their home areas and went together to Job to console/comfort him .
2.12: When they saw Job from a distance, they almost did not recognize him. They wailed loudly, they tore their robes, and they threw dust over their heads [to show how sorry they were because of what had happened to Job].

3.1: Finally, Job spoke, and he cursed the day that he was born.
3.3: “I wish that the day when I was born could be eradicated, and also the night when I was conceived.
3.4: I wish that the day when I was born would have been covered in darkness. I wish that God who is in heaven would have forgotten about that day, and that the sun would not have shone on it.
3.5: I wish that thick/intense darkness would have filled that day, and that a black cloud would have come over it and blotted out all light and caused people to be terrified.
3.6: I wish that the night when I was conceived would be erased from the calendar, with the result that it would never again appear as one night in any month, and that it would not be included in any calendar.
3.7: I wish that no child would again be conceived on that night of the month , and that no one would again be happy on that night.
3.8: I want those people who ◄curse/put evil spells on► days—those who know how to arouse/awaken the great sea monster—to curse that day.
3.9: I wish that the stars that shone early in the morning on that day [after I was conceived] will not shine again. I want those stars to have wished in vain for light to shine; and that they would not have shone on that day.
3.10: [That was an evil day] because my mother was able to conceive; instead, I was born, and I have now experienced all these terrible things.
3.11: “I wish that I had died when I was born— at the time I emerged from my mother’s womb.
3.12: I wish that my mother had not allowed me to live. I wish that she had not nursed me.
3.13: If I had died at the time when I was born, I would be asleep, resting peacefully i[in the place where the dead people are].
3.14: I would be resting with kings whose [beautiful palaces] that they built are now in ruins (OR, who rebuilt [palaces] that had previously been destroyed), and I would be resting with their officials [who have also died].
3.15: I would be resting with princes who were wealthy, whose palaces were filled with gold and silver.
3.16: I wish that I had been buried like a child who died in its mother’s womb and never lived to see the light.
3.17: After wicked people die, they do not cause any more troubles; those who are very tired now will rest.
3.18: Those who were in prison rest peacefully [after they die]; they no longer have slave-drivers who curse them.
3.19: Rich people and poor people are alike after they die, and those who were slaves are no longer controlled by their masters.
3.20: ◄“Why does God allow those who are suffering greatly [like me] to continue to remain alive?/I do not understand why God allows those who are suffering greatly [like me] to continue to remain alive.► Why does he allow those who are very miserable/distressed to keep living ?
3.21: They long/want to die, but they do not die. They desire to die more than people desire to find a hidden treasure.
3.22: When they finally die and are buried, they are very happy.
3.23: Those who do not know where they are [eventually] going when they die , people whom God has forced to continue to live in misery, ◄it is not right that they continue to live./why do they continue to live?►
3.24: I continually cry very much; as a result, I cannot eat; and I can never stop groaning.
3.25: Things that I always worried might happen to me, have happened to me; things that I always dreaded have happened to me.
3.26: Now I have no peace [in my inner being], I have no peace; I cannot rest; instead, I have only troubles.”

4.1: Then Eliphaz, from Teman, replied to Job. He said,
4.2: “Will you please let me say something to you? I am not able to remain silent [any longer].
4.3: In the past, you have instructed/taught many people, and you have encouraged those who were weak.
4.4: By what you said, you have helped those who ◄needed spiritual help/almost quit trusting in God► , and you have enabled them to become spiritually strong again .

4.6: You revere God; ◄does that not cause you to trust [in him]?/that should cause you to trust [in him].► If you were guiltless, you would be confident that [God] would not [have allowed] these disasters [to] happen to you!
4.7: Think about this: Do innocent people die [while they are still young] ? Does God get rid of godly people ? [No!]
4.8: What I have experienced is this: [Just as] farmers who plant bad [seeds] do not harvest good [crops], [just as those who start] trouble for others, later bring trouble on themselves.
4.9: They die when God angrily blows his breath on them, when he is very angry with them.

4.11: [They will die like] fierce lions [that] starve to death when there are no animals that they can kill and eat, and [their children will be separated from each other like] young lions separate from each other [to find food].”
4.12: “I heard a message that someone came and whispered to me.
4.13: He spoke to me at night when I was having a bad dream that disturbed/frightened me while I was fast asleep.
4.14: It caused me to be afraid and tremble; it caused all my bones to shake.
4.15: A ghost glided past my face and caused the hair on [on the back of] my neck to stand straight up.
4.16: It stopped, but I could not see what form it had. But [I could sense that] there was some being in front of me, and it said in a quiet voice,
4.17: ‘◄Does God consider anyone to be righteous?/No human beings can be righteous in God’s sight!► ◄Their creator cannot consider them to be pure./Can their creator consider them to be pure?►

4.21: They are like tents that collapse [suddenly]: They die [suddenly] before they become wise.’”

5.1: “Job, [it is okay that you] continue to cry out for someone to help you, but [I am certain that] no angel will come to help you!
5.2: Foolish people die because of being ◄resentful/very angry at someone►; people who are easily deceived are destroyed by their being jealous [of others].
5.3: I have seen foolish people who seemed to be successful/prosperous, but suddenly [they experienced disaster/trouble because] someone cursed their home.
5.4: Their sons are never safe; they ◄lose their case/are condemned► when someone ◄takes them to court/sues them►, because there is no one to defend them.
5.5: Hungry people [steal] the crops that foolish people harvest, [and] eat [those crops]; they even steal the crops that grow among thorns, and greedy people take away the wealth of foolish people.

5.23: You will not worry about [having big] rocks in your fields [that will make plowing difficult], and you will not worry about [being attacked by] wild animals there.

5.27: [“My friends and I] have thought carefully about these things, and [we know that] they are true, so pay attention to what I have said!”

6.1: Then Job spoke again, saying [to Eliphaz],
6.2: “If all my troubles and misery could be put on a scale and weighed,
6.3: they would be heavier than all the sands [on the shores] of the oceans. That is why I spoke ◄very rashly/without thinking clearly► [about the day that I was born].
6.4: [It is as though] Almighty [God] has shot me with arrows. [It is as though] those arrows had poison on their tips, and that poison has gone into my spirit. The things that God has done to me have terrified me.
6.5: Just like a wild donkey does not [complain by] braying when it has plenty of grass to eat, and an ox does not [complain by] bellowing when it has food to eat , [I would not complain if you were really helping/comforting me].
6.6: People complain when they must eat food which has no salt or other tasteless food , [and that is what your words are like, Eliphaz].

6.8: “I wish that God would do for me what I have requested from him .
6.9: I wish that he would crush me [and let me die]. I wish that he would reach out his hand and take away my life.
6.10: If he would do that, I would be comforted by knowing that in spite of the great pain that I have suffered, I have always obeyed what [God,] the Holy One, has commanded.

6.14: “When a man has many troubles, his friends should be kind to him, even if he stops revering Almighty [God].
6.15: But [you,] my friends, are not dependable. You are like streams: They spill over their banks [in the spring]
6.16: when [the melting] ice and snow make those streams overflow,
6.17: but when the dry season comes, there is no water flowing [in those streams], and the channels dry up.
6.18: [The caravans of merchants] turn off the path [to search for some water], but there is no water, so they die [in the desert].
6.19: The men in those caravans search [for some water] because they are sure that they will find some.
6.20: But they do not find any, so they are very disappointed.
6.21: Similarly, you friends have not helped me at all! You have seen that terrible things have happened to me, and you are afraid [that God might do similar things to you].
6.22: [After I lost all my wealth,] did I ask any of you for money? Did I plead with any of you to spend some of your money to help me ?
6.23: Have I asked any of you to rescue me from my enemies ? Have I asked you to save me from those who ◄oppressed me/treated me badly► ? [No!]”
6.24: “Answer me [now, and then] I will be quiet; tell me what wrong things I have done!
6.25: When people speak what is true, that will not hurt the person who hears it, but what you say, criticizing me, [is not true, so your saying it] proves nothing !

6.27: You do not sympathize with me at all [for all that I am suffering]. [You are heartless!] You would even gamble to see who gets an orphan [as a prize]!

7.1: “People need to work hard on this earth, like soldiers do; all during the time that we are alive, we work hard , like laborers/servants do.
7.2: We are like slaves who keep wanting to be in the cool shade, and we are like workers who are waiting to be paid.
7.3: God has given me many months [in which I think that it is] useless [to remain alive]; he has allotted/given to me many nights during which I feel miserable.
7.4: When I lie down [at night] I say, ‘How long will it be until morning?’ But nights are long, and I ◄toss/turn over and over► [on my bed] until dawn.
7.5: My body is covered with maggots and scabs; pus oozes out of my open sores.

7.7: God, do not forget that my life is [as short as] a breath ; I [think that] I will never again be happy.
7.8: God, you see me now, but [some day] you will not see me any more. You will search for me, but I will be gone [because I will be dead].
7.9: Like clouds ◄disperse/break up► and then disappear, people [die and] descend to the place where dead people are, and they do not return;
7.10: they never return to their houses, and people among whom they lived do not remember them any more.

7.12: [God,] why do you watch closely what I am doing? [Do you think that] I am a [dangerous] sea monster?
7.13: When [I lie down at night,] I think, ‘I will be comforted here on my bed; my pain will be less while I am sleeping.’
7.14: But then you give me dreams that cause me to be afraid; you give me visions that terrify me,
7.15: with the result that I would prefer to be strangled to death than to continue to [be alive] being only a bunch of bones.
7.16: I detest continuing to be alive; I do not want to live for many years . Allow me to be alone, [because I will be alive] for only a very short remaining time .
7.17: “We human beings are not [very important]; so, why do you pay a lot of attention to us ?
7.18: You look at us every morning [to see what we are doing], and examine us every moment [to see if we are doing what is right].
7.19: ◄When will you stop looking at me and leave me alone [for a little time], long enough to swallow my spit?/Please stop looking at me and leave me alone [for a little time], long enough to swallow my spit.►
7.20: [Why do] you watch me constantly? If I sin, that certainly does not harm you! Why have you set me up like a target to shoot at? Do you consider me to be a heavy load that you are forced to carry?
7.21: [If I have sinned,] are you not able to forgive me for my sins— the things that I have done that are wrong? Soon I will lie in my grave; you will search for me, but [you will not find me because] I will be [dead and] gone.”

8.1: Then Bildad, from [the] Shuah [area], spoke to Job. He said,

8.6: and if you are pure and honest/righteous, he will surely do something good for you and reward you by giving your family back to you and enabling you to prosper.
8.7: And even though you [think that you] were not very prosperous/wealthy before, during the last part of your life you will become very wealthy.
8.8: “I request you to think about what happened long ago and consider what our ancestors found out.

8.11: Papyrus can certainly not grow in places where there is no marsh/swamp; reeds certainly cannot flourish/grow where there is no water.
8.12: [If they do not have enough water], while they are still blossoming, they wither more quickly than other plants wither.
8.13: Those who do not pay attention to what God says are like those [reeds]; godless people stop confidently expecting [that good things will happen to them].
8.14: The things they confidently expect to happen do not happen; things they trust [will help them] are [as fragile as] a spider’s web.
8.15: If they lean against a house (OR, trust in their wealth; OR, lean on a spider web), it does not ◄endure/protect them► ; they cling to things [to be protected], but those things do not remain firm.
8.16: Godless people [are like plants] that are watered before the sun rises; their shoots spread all over the gardens.
8.17: The roots of those plants twist around piles of stones and cling tightly to rocks.
8.18: But if those plants are pulled out, [it is as though] the place where they were planted says ‘They were never here!’ [And that is what happens to wicked people who do not heed what God says].
8.19: Truly, evil people are not joyful for a long time; other people come and take their places.
8.20: :So, [I tell you, Job], God will not reject you if you are truly godly/righteous, but he does not help evil people.
8.21: He will enable you to continually laugh and to always shout [joyfully].
8.22: But those who hate you will be very ashamed, and the homes of wicked people will disappear.”

9.2: “Yes, I certainly know that [much of] what you said is true. But ◄how can anyone say to God, ‘I and prove it?’/no one can say to God ‘I and prove it.’►
9.3: If someone wanted to argue with God [about that], God could ask him 1,000 questions, and that person would not be able to answer any of them!
9.4: God is very wise and very powerful; no one who has tried to challenge God has been able to win.
9.5: He even moves mountains, without them (OR, anyone) knowing about it. When he is angry, he turns them upside down.
9.6: He sends earthquakes that shake the ground; he causes the pillars that support the earth to tremble.
9.7: [Some days] he speaks to the sun, and it does not rise, and [some nights] he prevents the stars from shining.
9.8: He alone ◄stretched out/put in place► the sky; he alone puts his feet on the waves (OR, on the huge sea monster).
9.9: He put in their places [the clusters/groups of stars that are called] The Dipper/Bear, Orion, the Pleiades, and the stars in the southern sky.
9.10: Only he does great things that we cannot understand; he does more marvelous things than we are able to count.
9.11: He passes by where I am, but I do not see him; he moves further on, but I do not see him go.
9.12: If he [wants to] snatch something away, no one can hinder him; no one dares to ask him, ‘Why are you doing that?’
9.13: God will not very easily stop being angry; he defeated those who [tried to] help Rahab, [the great sea monster].
9.14: “So, [if God took me to court], what could I say to answer him?
9.15: Even though I ◄would be innocent/would not have done what is wrong►, I would not be able to answer him. All I could do would be to request God, my judge/accuser, to act mercifully toward me.
9.16: If I summoned him to [come to the courtroom] and he said that he would come, I would not believe that he would pay attention to what I would say.
9.17: He sends storms to batter me, and he bruises me many times ◄without any reason to do that/even though I am innocent►.
9.18: [It is as though] he will not let me get/catch my breath, because he causes me to suffer all the time.
9.19: If I would try to ◄wrestle with/fight against► him, [there is no way that I could defeat him,] [because] he is stronger than I am. If I would request him to appear in court, there is no one who could force him to go there.
9.20: Even though I was innocent, what I would say would cause him to say that I must be punished ; even though I had not done anything wrong, he would prove that I am guilty.
9.21: “I have not done what is wrong, but that is not important. I despise continuing to remain alive.
9.22: But it doesn’t matter, because God will get rid of [all of us,] both those who are innocent and those who are wicked.
9.23: When people experience disaster and it causes them to suddenly die, God laughs at it, even if they are innocent.
9.24: God has allowed wicked people to control [what happens in] the world. [It is as though] he has caused judges to be blindfolded, [with the result that they cannot judge fairly]. If it is not God who has put wicked people in control, who has done it?
9.25: “My days go by very quickly, like a fast runner; [it is as though] they run away, and nothing good happens to me on those days.
9.26: My life goes by very rapidly, like a boat made from reeds sailing swiftly, or like an eagle that swoops down to seize a small animal.
9.27: If I smile and say [to God], ‘I will forget what I am complaining about; I will stop looking sad and try to be cheerful/happy,’

18.21: And that is what happens to ungodly/sinful people [like you], to people who ◄have no interest in/have rejected► God.”

19.2: “How long will you [three] torment me and crush my spirit by saying to me [that I am wicked]?
19.3: You have already insulted me many times; ◄are you not ashamed for saying these things to me?/you should be ashamed for saying these things to me.►
19.4: Even if it were true that I have done things that are wrong, I have not injured you!
19.5: If you truly think that you are better than I am, and you think that my being miserable now proves that I ◄am guilty/have committed many sins►,
19.6: you need to realize that it is God who has caused me to suffer. [It is as though] he has trapped me with his net.
19.7: “I cry out, ‘Help me!’, but no one answers me. I call out loudly, but there is no one, [not even God,] who acts fairly toward me.
19.8: [It is as though] God has blocked my way, with the result that I cannot go where I want to; [it is as though] he has forced me to try to find my way in the darkness.
19.9: He has ◄taken away my good reputation/caused people not to honor me any more►; [it is as though] he removed a crown from my head.
19.10: He batters me from every side, and I will soon die. He has caused me to no longer confidently expect [him to do good things for me].
19.11: He attacks me because he is extremely angry with me , and he considers that I am his enemy.
19.12: [It is as though] he sends his army to attack me; they surround my tent, preparing to attack me.
19.13: “God has caused my brothers to abandon me, and all those who know me act like strangers to me.
19.14: All my relatives and good friends have left me.
19.15: The people who were guests in my house have forgotten me, and my female servants consider that I am a stranger or that I am a foreigner.
19.16: When I summon my servants, they do not answer; I plead with them to come [to help me, but they do not come].
19.17: My wife does not want to come close to me because my breath [smells very bad], and even my brothers detest me.
19.18: Even young children despise me; when I stand up [to talk to them], they laugh at me.
19.19: My dearest friends detest me, and those whom I love [very much] have turned against me.
19.20: My body is [only] skin and bones; I am barely alive .
19.21: [“I plead with] you, my [three] friends, pity me, because God has ◄struck me with his hand/caused me to suffer greatly►.
19.22: Why do you cause me to suffer like God does? Why do you continue to slander me?
19.23: “I wish/desire that someone would take these words of mine and write them permanently in a book [in order that people can read them].
19.24: Or else, I wish that he would carve them on a rock with ◄a chisel/an iron tool► in order that they would last forever.
19.25: But I know that the one who vindicates/defends me in court is alive, and that some day he will stand [here] on the earth [and make the final decision about whether I deserve to be punished].
19.26: And even after diseases have eaten away my skin, while I still have my body, I will see God.
19.27: I will see him myself; I will see him with my own eyes! I am overwhelmed [as I think about that]!
19.28: “If you three men say, ‘What more can we do to cause Job to suffer?’ and if you say, ‘He has caused his own [troubles],’
19.29: you should be afraid that God will punish you; he punishes those [like you] with whom he is angry; and when that happens, you will know that there is [someone who] judges [people].”

20.2: “I am very perturbed about what you have said, so I want to reply very quickly.
20.3: By saying these things you have insulted me, but I know how (OR, because I understand very much) I can reply to you.
20.4: “Do you not know that from long ago, ever since people were first put on the earth,
20.5: wicked people [like you] do not continue to rejoice for a long time, ungodly people are happy only for a ◄moment/very short time► ?
20.6: [Even] though their reputation/pride reaches up to the sky and their fame goes up as high as the clouds,
20.7: they will disappear forever, like their own dung, and those who knew them will ask, ‘◄Where did they go/What happened to them►?’
20.8: They will be forgotten like a dream is, and they will exist no more. They will vanish, like visions [that people see] during the night.
20.9: Those who saw those people previously will never see them again; even their families will not see them any more.
20.10: Their children will be forced to return the valuable things that those children stole from poor people .
20.11: Previously their bodies were young and strong, but they will die and [their bodies will] be buried in the ground.
20.12: “Doing wicked things was like having sweet food in their mouths, and they wanted to continue to taste it.
20.13: And they did not want to stop doing those things,
20.14: [but some day] the evil things that they enjoyed doing will become like food [that they swallow] [and which becomes] as bitter as snake venom.
20.15: Wicked people will not continue to keep the money they have accumulated, like people do not keep the food that they vomit. God takes their wealth from them.
20.16: What wicked people do is [like] swallowing snake venom; it will kill them like the bite of a poisonous snake kills people.
20.17: They will not remain alive to see abundant blessings [from God], milk and olive oil and honey, that are [so abundant they are ] like a stream that flows by.
20.18: They will be forced to give back the things that they stole from the poor; they will not be able to continue to enjoy those things. They will not remain happy because of what they got from their businesses,
20.19: because they oppressed poor people and refused to help them, and they took other people’s houses [by cheating them].
20.20: “They were always greedy and never satisfied. They just keep dreaming about owning more and more things.
20.21: When they finished eating their food, there was never anything left over [because they had greedily eaten it all]; but now their prosperity will end.
20.22: When they are extremely prosperous/wealthy, they will suddenly experience a lot of trouble. ◄Misery will strike them and crush them /They will suffer very greatly►.
20.23: When the wicked people are filling their stomachs, God will show that he is very angry with them and punish them; the punishment [that he gives them] will be like rain falling on them.
20.24: They will try to escape from [being killed by] iron weapons, but arrows with bronze points will pierce them.
20.25: The arrows will [go completely through their bodies and] stick out of their backs; the shiny points of the arrows will have blood dripping from them, and those wicked people will be terrified.
20.26: Their valuable possessions will all be destroyed; a fire that is not lit by humans, [but by God,] will burn them up and also destroy the things that are left in their tents.
20.27: The [angels in] heaven will reveal the sins that those wicked people have committed, and [people on] earth will stand up and testify against them.
20.28: When God punishes [people], all the possessions in the wicked people’s houses will be carried away by a flood.
20.29: That is what will happen to wicked people [like you]; that is what God has decided will happen to them.”

21.2: “Listen to what I say, all [three] of you; that is the only thing that you can do that will comfort me.
21.3: Be patient with me, and allow me to speak. Then, after I am finished speaking, you can continue to make fun of me.
21.4: “It is certainly not people against whom I am complaining, [but God] And it is certainly right for me to be impatient!
21.5: Look at me! Does what you see not cause you to be appalled and to put your hands over your mouths [and say no more]?
21.6: When I think about [what has happened to me], I am frightened and my entire body shakes.
21.7: “[But let me ask this:] ‘Why do wicked people continue to live, and become prosperous, and not die until they are very old?’
21.8: They have their children around them, and they watch them while they [grow up and] start to live in their own houses, and they enjoy their grandchildren.
21.9: Wicked people live in their own houses without being afraid, and God does not punish them.
21.10: Their bulls always mate with the cows successfully, and the cows give birth to calves and never miscarry.
21.11: Wicked people send their young children outside [to play], and the children play [happily] like lambs [in a pasture].
21.12: Some children dance and sing, while others shake tambourines and play lyres, and they are happy when they hear people playing flutes.
21.13: Wicked people enjoy having good things all the time that they are alive, and they die quietly/peacefully and go down to the place of the dead.
21.14: While they are alive, they say to God, ‘Do not bother us; we do not want to know how you want us to conduct our lives!
21.15: Why do you, Almighty God, think that we should serve you? ◄What advantage do we get if we pray to you?/It is useless for us to pray to you.► ’
21.16: Think about it: Wicked people think that it is because of what they have done that they have become prosperous, but I do not understand why they think like that.
21.17: ◄“How often does it happen that wicked people die before they are old?/Very seldom do wicked people die before they are old.► ◄Do they ever experience disasters?/They seldom experience disasters.► ◄Does God ever punish them because of being very angry with them?/God never punishes them because of being very angry with them.►
21.18: [He does not blow] them away like wind blows away straw; they are never carried off by a whirlwind.
21.19: You say, ‘When people have committed sins, God waits and punishes their children because of those sins;’ but [I say that] God should punish those who sin, [not their children,] in order that the sinners will know [that it is because of their own sins that they are being punished].
21.20: I hope/wish that wicked people will experience themselves being destroyed, that they will experience being punished by an angry Almighty God.
21.21: After wicked people are dead, they are not at all concerned about what happens to their families .
21.22: “Since God judges [everyone,] even those that are in heaven, ◄who can teach God anything?/certainly no one can teach God anything.►
21.23: Some people die while they are very healthy, while they are peaceful, when they are not afraid of anything.
21.24: Their bodies are fat; their bones are strong.
21.25: Other people die being very miserable; they have never experienced good things happening to them.
21.26: But both rich and poor people die and are buried, and maggots eat their bodies. [Everyone dies, so it is clear that dying is not always the punishment for being wicked].
21.27: “Listen, I know what you [three] are thinking. I know the evil things that you plan to do to me.
21.28: You say, ‘What happened to the tents in which wicked people were living? The houses of evil rulers have been destroyed!’
21.29: But have you never inquired of people who travel much? Do you not believe their reports about what they have seen,
21.30: that wicked people usually do not suffer at the time when there are great disasters; that wicked people are the ones who are rescued when God is angry [and punishes people] ?
21.31: There is no one who accuses wicked people, and there is no one who ◄pays them back/gives them the punishment that they deserve► for all the evil things that they have done.
21.32: The corpses of wicked people are carried to their graves, and people are put there to guard those graves.
21.33: A huge number of people go to the grave site. Some go in front of the procession and some come behind. And the clods of dirt thrown on the graves of those wicked people who have died are like a nice blanket.
21.34: “So how can you console me by talking nonsense? Every reply that you make is full of lies!”

22.2: “◄Can anyone be useful to God?/Certainly no one can be useful to God.► Even people who are wise cannot be helpful to God.
22.3: If you were righteous, ◄would that benefit Almighty [God]?/that certainly would not benefit Almighty [God].► If you had ◄lived a perfect life/never done anything that is wrong►, would that help him?
22.4: “Is it because you have an awesome respect for God that he punishes you? Is that the reason that he puts you on trial?
22.5: No, it certainly must be because you are extremely wicked. It must be that the evil things that you have done are so many that no one can count them!
22.6: You must have lent money to others and wrongly forced them to give you things to guarantee that they would pay that money back to you; you must have taken all their clothes and left them with nothing to wear.
22.7: You must not have given water to those who were thirsty, and you must have refused to give food to those who were hungry.
22.8: Because you were very powerful, you [must have] taken over all the people’s land, and then, being very respected, you have begun to live on that land.
22.9: [When] widows [came to you for help], you [must have] sent [them] away without giving them anything, and you must have oppressed orphans.
22.10: Because of all that, now there are pits around you for you to fall into, and suddenly there are things that terrify you and cause you to tremble.
22.11: [It is as though] it has become very dark, with the result that you cannot see anything, and [it is as though] a flood covers you.
22.12: “[But consider this, Job]: God lives high up in the heavens. From there he looks down on the highest stars.
22.13: So why do you say, ‘What does God know [about what we are doing]? [He is hidden from us by] dark clouds, so ◄[how] can he judge us?/he certainly cannot judge us.► ’
22.14: [Do you think that] while he walks on the dome that covers the sky, there are thick clouds around him, with the result that he cannot see [what we do]?
22.15: Will you continue to conduct your life the old way that evil people have done [for many years]?
22.16: They suddenly died while they were still young; they disappeared [like everything disappears when there is] a flood .
22.17: They kept saying to God, ‘Do not bother us,’ and they also said [defiantly], ‘Almighty [God] can do nothing to [harm] us!’
22.18: But it was God who filled their houses with good things, so I cannot at all understand why wicked people think like they do.
22.19: “But when God punishes wicked people, and righteous people see that, they are glad, and they laugh, ridiculing the wicked people.
22.20: They say, ‘Now our enemies have been destroyed, and all [their possessions] that were left have been burned in a fire.’
22.21: “So, [Job,] be reconciled to God and make peace with him; if you do that, good things will happen to you.
22.22: Allow him to teach you, and keep thinking about what he has told you.
22.23: If you humble yourself and return to God, if you stop doing all the evil things that you have been doing in your house,
22.24: if you throw away your gold, even the fine gold from the dry stream beds in Ophir [land],
22.25: and if you allow Almighty [God] to be [as precious to you as] your gold and your silver [have been],
22.26: you will be happy because of your close relationship with God, and you will be able to approach him [confidently].
22.27: You will pray to him, and he will do what you request him to do; you will do the things that you promised him that you would do.
22.28: Everything that you decide to do will be successful; [it] will [be as though] a light [is] shining on the road in front of you.
22.29: God humbles those who are proud, but he saves those who are downcast/discouraged.
22.30: God rescues those who ◄are innocent/have not done things that are wrong►, so he will rescue you if you ◄start doing things that are right/are not guilty of doing things that are wrong►.”

23.2: “Today I am again complaining bitterly/strongly [to God]; I [continue] groaning, but he [continues to] ◄punish me/cause me to suffer►.
23.3: I ◄wish that I knew/want to know► where I could meet/talk with him, so that I could go to the place where he lives.
23.4: If I could do that, I would tell him why [I know that] I am innocent; I would tell to him all my ◄arguments/evidence [to show that I have not done what is evil]►.
23.5: Then I would find out what he would reply to me .
23.6: Would he use his great power to argue with me? No, he would listen to me carefully.
23.7: I am ◄an honest/a righteous► man; so I would be able to discuss things with him [fairly], and then he would declare that I am innocent, [and that decision would endure] forever.
23.8: “But, I have gone to the east, and he is not there; I have gone to the west, but I have not found him there.
23.9: I have gone north and I have gone south, but I have not seen him anywhere.
23.10: But he knows how I have conducted my life; and when he has finished testing me, [he] will [see that] I [am] as pure as gold [whose impurities have all been burned out].
23.11: I have faithfully walked on the path that he showed me; I have not stopped [obeying] him.
23.12: I have always obeyed what he commanded; I have treasured the words that he has spoken.
23.13: “He never changes. There is no one who can stop him [from doing what he desires]. Whatever he wants to do, he does.
23.14: And he will finish doing for me the things that he has planned for me; [and I am sure that] he has thought about doing many things for me.
23.15: So I am terrified in his presence; when I think [about what he can do], I am very afraid .
23.16: Almighty God has caused me to feel terrified .
23.17: [It is as though] there is only thick darkness in front of me, but it is God that I am afraid of, not the darkness.”

24.1: “◄Why does Almighty [God] not set a time when he will judge [evil people]?/I do not understand why Almighty [God does] not set a time when he will judge [evil people].► Those who know him never see him do that!
24.2: [Some evil people] remove the markers of boundaries of [other people’s] land, [in order to steal their land]; they seize/steal [other people’s] sheep and put them in their own pastures.
24.3: [Some] ◄take away/steal► the donkeys that belong to orphans, and they take widow’s oxen to guarantee that the widows will pay back the money that they loaned to those widows.
24.4: [Some] shove poor people off the road (OR, prevent poor people from ◄obtaining their rights/being treated justly►), and they force poor people to find places to hide from them.
24.5: The result is that poor people have to search for food in the desert like wild donkeys do.
24.6: The poor people harvest left-over grain in other people’s fields, and gather grapes from vineyards that belong to wicked men.
24.7: During the night they have nothing to cover their bodies, nothing to keep them warm.
24.8: When it rains on the mountains, the poor people become very wet, so they huddle under the rock ledges to be protected [from the rain].
24.9: [Some evil men] snatch infants away from their widowed mothers , and they say ‘I will return your babies to you when you repay the money that I lent to you.’
24.10: But the poor people walk around with no clothes on; they are hungry while they are working to carry [other people’s] bundles of grain [to the places where their grain will be threshed].
24.11: Poor people press olives to make [olive] oil; they tread on grapes [to make juice for wine], but [they are not allowed to drink any of it when] they become thirsty.
24.12: In the cities, people who are wounded and dying cry out [to God for help], but God does not heed their prayers.
24.13: Some wicked people avoid the light [because they do evil things in the dark]; they do not walk on roads that are lighted.
24.14: Murderers steal things during the night, and then they arise before dawn in order that they may [go out again and] kill needy people.
24.15: Those who want to commit adultery wait for twilight/evening; they say ‘I do not want anyone to see me,’ so they keep their faces covered.
24.16: It is during the night that robbers break into houses [to steal things], but during the day they hide because they want to avoid [being seen in] the light.
24.17: All of those [people] want to do their evil things at night, not in the morning [when it is light], because they are not afraid of [the things that happen during the] night that terrify others.”
24.18: “[But it is wicked people] who are swept/carried away by floods, and God curses the land that they own, and no one goes to work in their vineyards.
24.19: Just like the snow melts away when it is hot and there is no rain, those who have sinned disappear into the place where dead people are.
24.20: Not even their mothers remember them now; wicked people are destroyed like trees that are cut down, and maggots eat their corpses.
24.21: They mistreat women who have been unable to give birth to children and women who no longer have children [to take care of them], and they never do good things for widows.
24.22: But God, by his power, gets rid of mighty/influential people. God acts and causes the wicked people to die.
24.23: God allows them to think that they are secure and safe, but he is watching them all the time.
24.24: They prosper for a little while, and then [suddenly] they are gone; they disappear like weeds wither and die; they are like stalks of grain that have been cut off.
24.25: If this is not true, is there anyone who will show that I am a liar and prove that what I have said is not true?”

25.2: “God is very powerful; everyone should have an awesome respect for him; he causes everything to be peaceful high up in heaven.
25.3: ◄Can anyone count the angels who are in his army [in heaven]?/No one can count the angels who are in his army [in heaven].► ◄Is there any place where his light does not shine?/There is no place where his light does not shine.►
25.4: So, ◄how can God consider anyone to be righteous?/God certainly cannot consider anyone to be righteous.► ◄How can any human being be truly pure?/No human being can be truly pure.►
25.5: Consider this: God does not even consider the full moon to be bright, and he does not consider the stars to be spotless.
25.6: So, ◄what about humans?/he does not consider humans [to be important].► They are [as insignificant as] maggots. [God does not think more highly of] people [than he thinks of] worms.”

26.2: “I am a very weak and helpless man; and ◄you [certainly] have not helped me very much!/[do you think that] you have helped me very much?►
26.3: ◄You certainly have counseled me well—I, who am not wise at all./[Do you think that] you have counseled me well—I, who am not wise at all?► ◄[I’m sure you think that] you have given a lot of very good advice to me.
26.4: Who helped you to say all those [great/wise] things? Who inspired you to speak like you did?”
26.5: “[Because] the spirits of dead people [are afraid], [they] tremble in the waters that are deep under the earth.
26.6: God knows all about [those who are in] the place of the dead; there is nothing down there that prevents God from seeing what is there.
26.7: God stretched out the earth over the huge empty space and caused the earth to have nothing [to support it].
26.8: He fills the thick/dense clouds with water and prevents that water from bursting the clouds.
26.9: He causes clouds to ◄obscure/prevent us from seeing► the moon.
26.10: He separated the light from the darkness and put the horizon to mark the place where the night ends and the daytime begins.
26.11: When [he is angry, it is as though] he rebukes the pillars that hold up the sky. They are ◄shocked/very fearful►, and they tremble.
26.12: With his power he calmed the sea; with his skill/wisdom he destroyed Rahab, the huge sea monster.
26.13: With his breath he caused the sky to be bright/clear; with his hand he killed the great dragon in the sea.
26.14: But those events show only a small amount of his power; [it is as though] we are hearing only whispers of his powerful voice. When we hear thunder, [we say,] ‘◄Who can really understand [how great] his power [is]/No one can [really] understand [how great] his power [is]!► ’”

27.1: Job replied again [to his three friends],
27.2: “Almighty God has refused to treat me justly/fairly. He has caused me to feel bitter/resentful. But [just as surely] as he lives,
27.3: as long as God’s Spirit enables me to breathe,
27.4: I will not lie; I will not say anything to deceive anyone.
27.5: I will never admit that what you [three] have said is true; until the day that I die, I will insist that I have not done things that are wrong.
27.6: I will say that I am innocent, and never ◄say anything different/change what I say►; my conscience will never reproach me as long as I live.
27.7: “I want my enemies to be [punished] like all wicked [people are punished]; I want [God to punish] those who oppose me like [he punishes all] unrighteous [people].
27.8: When [it is time for] God [to] get rid of godless/wicked people and [to] cause them to die, there is absolutely nothing good that they can confidently expect [to happen to them].
27.9: When they experience troubles, ◄will God hear them call [out to him for help]?/God certainly will not hear them call out [to him for help].►
27.10: ◄Will they be happy about what Almighty [God] does?/They certainly will not be happy about what Almighty [God] does.► ◄Will they [begin to] pray to him frequently?/They certainly will not [begin to] pray to him frequently.► [Certainly not!]
27.11: “I will teach you [three] something about the power of Almighty God ; I will reveal what he is thinking.
27.12: But you [three] have seen for yourselves [what God has done]; so ◄why are you saying such nonsense?/you should not be saying such nonsense.►
27.13: “[I will tell you] what Almighty God does to wicked people, the things that he does to people who oppress others.
27.14: [Even] if they have many children, [many of] those children will die in wars , and their [other] children will [die because they do] not have enough food to eat.
27.15: Their children who are still alive will die from diseases, and their widows will not [even] mourn for them.
27.16: Sometimes [wicked people] accumulate a huge amount of silver and pile up clothes like those clothes were a pile of clay,
27.17: but [those wicked people will die, and then] righteous people will wear those clothes, and honest/innocent people will get their silver and divide it [among themselves].
27.18: The houses that they build are [as frail/fragile] as spider webs, or they are like flimsy huts that watchmen live in [while they guard people’s fields].
27.19: Wicked people are rich when they lie down [at night], but when they wake up [in the morning, they find out that] their money has disappeared.
27.20: “Things that terrify them strike them like a flood ; during the night a whirlwind carries them away.
27.21: [It is as though] the wind from the east picks them up and carries them away from their homes, and they disappear.
27.22: That wind strikes them without pitying them while they are running away, trying to escape from its force/power .
27.23: That wind [is like someone] clapping his hands at them [to ridicule them], howling at them wherever they run to.”

28.1: “It is true that there are places where men dig to find silver, and there are places where people refine/purify gold [that they have dug].
28.2: People dig iron [ore] out of the ground, and they ◄smelt copper ore/heat copper ore to get the copper from it►.
28.3: Men use lamps while they work far down under the ground to search for the ore inside the mines where it is very dark.
28.4: They dig ◄shafts/narrow holes very deep down into the ground► in places that are far from where people live, where travelers do not go. They work far away from [other] people, swinging back and forth on ropes [as they descend into the mine shafts].
28.5: Food grows on the surface of the ground, but down under the ground, [where there is no food,] the miners make fires to break apart the rocks.
28.6: The stones [that are dug from under the ground] contain ◄sapphires/very valuable blue stones►, and the dirt contains bits of gold.
28.7: [Some birds have very good eyes,] but even hawks do not know [where the mines are], and falcons/vultures have not seen those places.
28.8: Lions or [other] proud wild animals have not walked on the roads near those mines.
28.9: Miners tear apart very hard rock; [it is as though] they turn the mountains upside down [to get the ore].
28.10: They cut tunnels through the rocks, and they find ◄precious/very valuable► things.
28.11: They dam up small streams in order that water does not flow, and they bring up into the light valuable things that are hidden [in the ground and in the streams].
28.12: “But wisdom: Where can people find that? Where can we find out how to truly understand things?
28.13: Humans do not know where to find it; no one can find it [here on this earth] where they are living.
28.14: [It is as though] water that is deep [inside the earth] and [water that is in] the seas say , ‘Wisdom is not here!’
28.15: [People] cannot buy wisdom by paying for it with silver or gold.
28.16: Wisdom is worth much more than fine gold from Ophir [land] or other very valuable stones.
